transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-25
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Miller (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (NovaApps CTO), Maya Patel (NovaApps ML Eng), Samir Khan (NovaApps Product)

[00:00] Sofia Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, I'm the AE on this deal, and with me is Daniel our SE. Hi Daniel.
[00:07] Daniel Park: Hi all, thanks for having us. Excited to walk through the migration mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood.
[00:12] Jared Liu: Hi, Jared here. Quick note, we're on PST, so forgive any background noise, we got a sprint wrap behind us.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Hey, Maya. I'll focus on the ML side and share the prompt examples we run in prod.
[00:22] Samir Khan: Samir from product, mostly listening for infra and cost implications.

[00:30] Sofia: Goal for today is twofold: show parity for the most-used APIs \u2014 text gen/chat/embeddings and function calling \u2014 and call out where behavior differs or where Redwood gives additional controls like routing, caching, quantization recs.
[00:45] Maya: Sounds good. Our immediate ask is that we don't regress on output fidelity; cost is secondary but important. We have ~2k token avg prompts and a few long-completion flows to 6k.

[01:05] Daniel: Great, so first, quick mapping table: OpenAI completion -> Redwood text.generate; Chat API -> Redwood chat.create; embeddings -> embeddings.create. Function calling patterns map similarly but note Redwood uses the same schema for tool/formats but requires explicit schema registration in the Console for stronger type enforcement.
[01:30] Maya: Ah is that optional? We currently rely on dynamic function payloads.
[01:36] Daniel: You can keep dynamic calls, but registering schemas gives you stronger validation, which helps in our Optimize tooling to detect regressions. Also, it enables faster KV cache hits for repeated structured calls.

[02:10] [crosstalk]
[02:15] Sofia: We'll show a live example \u2014 Daniel will start the demo with a side-by-side of an OpenAI call and Redwood equivalent.

[02:30] Daniel: Opening the demo app. OK, here's an OpenAI call we run: prompt with system+user, model gpt-4o \u2014 returns streaming tokens. On the Redwood side we flip to text.generate with model redwood-4o-compat and enable streaming=true, delta mode. You'll see we support chunked streaming with identical token deltas.
[03:00] Maya: Any differences in chunk boundaries? We measure throughput at 50ms latency per chunk currently.
[03:08] Daniel: Chunk boundaries can differ slightly due to tokenization and the runtime's decoding strategy, but typically within the same order. We've seen parity in quality in our bench tests; we'll run your dataset to be sure.

[03:40] Daniel: Now function calling \u2014 OpenAI's 'function_call' param maps to Redwood's 'tools' parameter. Example: a weather tool registration. Redwood returns structured JSON and sets a tool_invocation meta field. Slight differences: we require tool schemas to be uploaded for best validation, otherwise it behaves like dynamic function
[04:05] Jared: How about ambiguous calls where multiple tools match? OpenAI tends to pick one; do you have tie-breakers?
[04:12] Daniel: We route based on tool priority and can configure disambiguation policies in Console; you can also enable a 'suggest' mode instead of auto-invoke.

[04:40] Sofia: Let's talk embeddings mapping \u2014 you call embeddings.create with model 'text-embedding-3' \u2014 Redwood embedding models map 1:1 in our catalog (e.g., redwood-embed-3). We also provide batch endpoints and a memory optimized variant for lower-latency small batches.
[05:05] Maya: We do 512-d vectors and use cosine; any format diffs?
[05:10] Daniel: No diffs, vectors are plain floats, same dims. We return base64 or arrays depending on your SDK choice.

[05:30] [15 sec silence, background noise]

[05:50] Daniel: Rate limits \u2014 Redwood enforces per-account throughput; for migration we can mirror your current soft-limits and then tune. For high-throughput pipelines we suggest Dedicated for predictable QPS, otherwise hosted with burst.
[06:10] Samir: Cost \u2014 can you show a quick cost comparison for 2k token prompts?
[06:18] Daniel: Rough example: with batching and prefix caching you often see 30-50% lower per-token cost vs naive OpenAI depending on quantization and model. We'll produce a cost matrix with your prompt mix.

[06:45] Sofia: Security \u2014 we support SOC2, SSO/SAML, per-route RBAC, VPC Peering for Private deployments, and KMS integrations for key management. Daniel has the security pack; we'll send it after.
[07:05] Jared: Do you log prompt text? We have privacy constraints and need redaction options.
[07:10] Daniel: By default we store minimal metadata; you can opt out of storing full transcripts and enable server-side find/redaction; for Dedicated/Private you control logs entirely.

[07:30] Maya: Technical deep dive \u2014 we have some performance concerns for 6k token flows.
[07:35] Daniel: For long sequences we recommend split-prefix caching and larger KV-cache config; we can also suggest quant profiles that keep quality while reducing GPU memory and cost. On Dedicated we can pin a longer-context instance.

[08:00] [Demo continues \u2014 code snippets shown]
[08:12] Daniel: Here's a parity example in Node: OpenAI code on left, Redwood SDK on right. Most calls are 1:1, auth header change, endpoints, and minor param renames. Example: OpenAI's max_tokens -> Redwood's max_output_tokens. Stop tokens behave the same.
[08:42] Maya: Will the SDK change our error handling? We currently check for rate-limit X-Rate-Limit headers.
[08:48] Daniel: We expose similar headers and also a per-token billing header so you can instrument cost in-app.

[09:10] Sofia: Let's cover known gaps \u2014 we don't have an exact clone of Anthropic's style steer tooling. Instead we provide programmatic style controls plus our Optimize layer that can run prompt evals to detect regression.
[09:30] Maya: So we'd lose some Anthropic style tuning?
[09:34] Daniel: Not necessarily lose, just different levers. You can implement safety layers with our toolchain and run post-hoc filters in the Console.

[10:00] [11:00 minutes later \u2014 timestamps a bit sparse to simulate imperfect transcription]
[11:05] Daniel: About deployment modes: Hosted API for quick migration, Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation, and Private for VPC/on-prem. For your compliance needs we recommend Private if you need full network isolation.
[11:26] Jared: If we start hosted then shift to Dedicated, will we need to re-instrument?
[11:30] Daniel: No \u2014 same API and SDK. You can pin model versions and change routing policies in Console; rollout can be canaryed.

[12:05] Samir: Any tooling to detect regression when we switch models?
[12:10] Daniel: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports prompt sets, evals, and regression alerts; we'll map your critical prompts into evals and set thresholds.

[12:30] Maya: Benchmarks \u2014 we want to run our test suite. What's needed?
[12:34] Daniel: Share a representative dataset (anonymized), and we'll run a comparison across your current models and Redwood-compat variants. We'll need API keys and preferred region.
[12:45] Maya: We'll share next day.

[13:05] Sofia: Ok quick recap and open floor.
[13:10] Jared: One last question about function calling and the tool priority \u2014 if we have proprietary tools we need to ensure no cross-tenant leakage.
[13:18] Daniel: Tools are per-tenant and per-model registration; no cross-tenant invocation. We also recommend dedicated pools for strict isolation.

[13:40] Samir: Great \u2014 can you also show cost implications for our 2k avg prompt and the 6k outliers?
[13:46] Daniel: Yes, we'll produce a cost/latency matrix as part of the follow-up.

[14:00] [Closing]
[14:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone. Next steps: Sofia will send parity mapping doc and SDK snippets, Daniel will send security pack and run initial bench once we get the sample dataset. We'll provision a trial quota for Dedicated so you can run tests. Any objections?
[14:20] Maya: No objections. Thanks.
[14:22] Jared: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription includes small mis-hears \u2014 'redwood' sometimes capitalized oddly in transcript artifacts. Links shared: parity_mapping_spreadsheet.xlsx (link), security_pack_v2.pdf (link), demo_recording_link (link).
